newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MALTA MATCH REVIVES FOND MEMORIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALTA MATCH REVIVES FOND MEMORIES.

text.p: Even laid back commentator Angel de la Casa was caught up in the emotion of the occasion.
Spain, needing to beat Malta by 10 goals to qualify for the 1984 European championhip finals at the expense of the Netherlands, won 12-1 in Seville.

"People often remind me of the way my voice cracked at the last goal. It's the only time it's happened...but it was so impossible what the team achieved that I was affected by the atmosphere," said de la Casa.
The game has become the stuff of legend in Spain and is bound to be relived when the two sides meet in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
The thumping win helped seal the reputation of Seville as an impregnable bastion for the national side.
It also helped to restore the game's image in Spain after a disastrous World Cup two years earlier.
"That game was the resurrection of Spanish football after its death in the World Cup. That night we recovered our pride," said de la Casa.
Spain went on to reach the final in Paris but lost 2-0 to France.
